title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 104
paragraphs: The Cypriots too, except for those of Amathus, were added voluntarily to their alliance; for these also had revolted from the Medes in the following way. There was a certain Onesilus, younger brother of Gorgus king of Salamis, and son of Chersis, the son of Siromus, the son of Euelthon. This man, too, had often in the past advised Gorgus to revolt from the king, and now, when he heard that the Ionians had revolted, he pressed him hard and tried to urge him to it. When he could not persuade Gorgus, Onesilus watched for a time when Gorgus had gone out of the city of Salamis, and then together with the men of his own faction he shut him out of the gates. Gorgus, robbed of the city, took refuge with the Medes, and Onesilus became ruler of Salamis and tried to persuade all the men of Cyprus to join him in revolt. Most he persuaded; but since those of Amathus were not willing to do as he wished, he sat down before their city and besieged it.
